forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {懐|なつ}いていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to become attached to; to take to; to warm up to
definitions.explanation: To develop affection and trust toward someone, becoming comfortable in their presence. Most commonly used for animals becoming tame and friendly with a person, or for young children warming up to an adult.

examples.japanese: この{猫|ねこ}はすぐに{懐|なつ}いた。
examples.english: This cat warmed up to me right away.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{子|こ}どもが{私|わたし}に{懐|なつ}いて、{毎日|まいにち}{遊|あそ}びに{来|く}る。
examples.english: The neighborhood kid has taken a liking to me and comes to play every day.

examples.japanese: {野良猫|のらねこ}にエサをあげていたら、だんだん{懐|なつ}いてきて、{今|いま}では{膝|ひざ}の{上|うえ}に{乗|の}るようになった。
examples.english: I kept feeding a stray cat, and it gradually warmed up to me — now it sits on my lap.

notes:
USAGE:
Primarily used for animals and small children, not for adult-to-adult relationships. The subject is the one becoming attached (the animal or child), and the person they warm up to is marked with に.

Pattern: [animal/child]が[person]に{懐|なつ}く

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猫|ねこ}が{懐|なつ}く (a cat warms up to someone)
- {犬|いぬ}が{懐|なつ}く (a dog takes to someone)
- {子|こ}どもが{懐|なつ}く (a child becomes attached)
- すぐに{懐|なつ}く (to warm up quickly)
- なかなか{懐|なつ}かない (to not easily warm up)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {慣|な}れる: to get used to — broader; about becoming accustomed, not necessarily affectionate
- {甘|あま}える: to act spoiled, to be clingy — the behavior that follows after {懐|なつ}く
